column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:io module
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Loadable module of input/output words that were moved out of the core
# registry. Most are reached only after `import`, under the `IO`
# namespace: `import "aql:io" IO.word args`. `print` is NOT here — it
# stays a core word so basic output needs no import.
# FILE I/O IS PATHON-ONLY. Every filesystem target is a `Scalar/Micron/
# Pathon` built with `make Pathon "…"` — a bare string is refused, so a
# file target is type-distinct from an arbitrary string and from a stream
# handle. A word that returns its target returns that Pathon (rendered
# without quotes), so `IO.read (IO.write p x)` threads through.
# `list` and `remove` are the exception to the namespace rule: aql:io
# extends the CORE `list` / `remove` words with a Pathon overload, so
# after import the BARE words gain filesystem behaviour — `list p` /
# `remove p` — rather than a separate `IO.list` / `IO.remove` (see
# design/OPEN-WORDS.0.md). The overload only registers on import.
# §1  stream handles — `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr` are ATOMs of the
#     StreamKind type (a closed enumeration of exactly those three, not
#     strings). StreamKind is exported by this module — `IO.StreamKind`,
#     not a global builtin.
import "aql:io" IO.stdout
column3: standard-output handle is the `stdout` atom

column1: import "aql:io" IO.stderr
column3: standard-error handle is the `stderr` atom

column1: import "aql:io" typeof IO.stdin
column3: a stream handle's type is StreamKind

column1: import "aql:io" IO.stdin is IO.StreamKind
column3: stdin inhabits the StreamKind type

column1: import "aql:io" IO.stdout is IO.StreamKind
column3: stdout inhabits the StreamKind type

column1: import "aql:io" IO.stderr is IO.StreamKind
column3: stderr inhabits the StreamKind type

column1: import "aql:io" stdin/q is IO.StreamKind
column3: a bare `stdin` atom is admitted too

column1: import "aql:io" foo/q is IO.StreamKind
column3: an unrelated atom is NOT a StreamKind

column1: import "aql:io" "stdout" is IO.StreamKind
column3: the STRING "stdout" is not a StreamKind

column1: # §2  trace — run a list as a traced sub-program, returning its result
import "aql:io" IO.trace [1 add 2 mul 3]
column3: traced evaluation returns the value

column1: # §3  negative — the words are gone from core (unbound without import)
read "x"
column3: `read` is no longer a core word

column1: folder "x"
column3: `folder` (filesystem op) also moved to aql:io

column1: IO.stdout
column3: `IO` is unbound without `import`

column1: # §3a  Pathon-only — a STRING target is refused; the caller supplies a Pathon
import "aql:io"  IO.read "data.csv"
column3: a String read target no longer matches — file I/O is Pathon-only

column1: import "aql:io"  IO.write "out.txt" "hi"
column3: a String write target is refused too

column1: # §4  printstr / stdin — output a value without a newline; the stdin handle
import "aql:io"  IO.printstr "hi"
column3: printstr writes formatted text to output, leaving no value

column1: import "aql:io"  IO.stdin
column3: standard-input handle is the `stdin` atom

column1: # §5  read / write against an in-memory filesystem
#     `context get __sys get fs set mem true` switches the FileOps capability
#     to an in-memory backing, so write-then-read is deterministic here.
#     `make Pathon "mem://b.txt"` collapses to the Pathon `mem:/b.txt`.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://b.txt") "hi"
column3: write returns the Pathon it wrote

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.read (IO.write (make Pathon "mem://a.txt") "hello")
column3: read back the bytes just written

column1: # §6  writing NON-STRING data needs no options map, reading a stream that is
#     not stdin errors, and StreamKind-tagged write returns the handle — all
#     runtime behaviours exercised in lang/go/native/io_stream_test.go and
#     fileio_test.go (they return Any / raise runtime-only errors, which do
#     not belong on the static-checker spec surface).
# §8  stat — describe a Pathon, returning a FileInfo record (name/path/type/
#     size/mode/mtime, plus target for a symlink), or `none` when absent.
#     `type` is an IO.FileType atom (file/dir/symlink/other).
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://s.txt") "hello" drop  (IO.stat (make Pathon "mem://s.txt")).size
column3: stat reports a file's byte size

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://s.txt") "x" drop  (IO.stat (make Pathon "mem://s.txt")).type
column3: stat's type field is a FileType atom

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://s.txt") "x" drop  (IO.stat (make Pathon "mem://s.txt")).type is IO.FileType
column3: the type field inhabits IO.FileType

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  file/q is IO.FileType
column3: a bare `file` atom is a FileType

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  "file" is IO.FileType
column3: the STRING "file" is not a FileType

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.stat (make Pathon "mem://ghost.txt")
column3: stat of an absent path is none

column1: # §9  list — the CORE `list` word, EXTENDED by aql:io with a Pathon overload:
#     `list p` enumerates a directory's entries (names, or records with
#     {detail:true}); {recursive:true} walks the tree. It is a BARE word
#     after import, not IO.list. Listing a missing directory or a file errors.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://L/a.txt") "x" drop  list (make Pathon "mem://L")
column3: list returns entry names

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  list (make Pathon "mem://nope")
column3: listing an absent directory errors

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  list (IO.write (make Pathon "mem://f.txt") "x")
column3: listing a file (not a directory) errors

column1: list (make Pathon "mem://X")
column3: the Pathon overload is absent without `import "aql:io"`

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://L/a.txt") "x" drop  IO.list (make Pathon "mem://L")
column3: the same handler is also reachable namespaced as IO.list

column1: # §10  remove — the CORE `remove` word, EXTENDED by aql:io with a Pathon
#      overload: `remove p` deletes a path, returning it. {recursive:true}
#      removes a directory tree; {force:true} makes an absent removal a no-op.
#      A bare word after import, not IO.remove.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://R/a.txt") "x" drop  remove (make Pathon "mem://R/a.txt")
column3: remove returns the deleted Pathon

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  remove (make Pathon "mem://ghost.txt")
column3: removing an absent path errors

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://k.txt") "x" drop  remove (make Pathon "mem://ghost.txt") {force:true}
column3: {force:true} makes an absent removal a no-op

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://R2/a.txt") "x" drop  IO.remove (make Pathon "mem://R2/a.txt")
column3: the same handler is also reachable namespaced as IO.remove

column1: # §11  move — rename/move a Pathon, returning the destination Pathon.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://m.txt") "x" drop  IO.move (make Pathon "mem://m.txt") (make Pathon "mem://m2.txt")
column3: move returns the destination

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.move (make Pathon "mem://ghost.txt") (make Pathon "mem://z.txt")
column3: moving an absent path errors

column1: # §12  copy — copy a Pathon to a destination. {recursive:true} copies a tree.

import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://c.txt") "hi" drop  IO.copy (make Pathon "mem://c.txt") (make Pathon "mem://c2.txt") drop  IO.read (make Pathon "mem://c2.txt")
column3: copy duplicates a file's contents

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://cd/a.txt") "x" drop  IO.copy (make Pathon "mem://cd") (make Pathon "mem://cd2")
column3: copying a directory without {recursive} errors

column1: # §13  link — create a link at dst referring to src: a symlink by default,
#      a hard link with {hard:true}. Returns the link Pathon.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.link (make Pathon "mem://target.txt") (make Pathon "mem://sl")
column3: link returns the created link path

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://h.txt") "hi" drop  IO.link (make Pathon "mem://h.txt") (make Pathon "mem://h2") {hard:true} drop  IO.read (make Pathon "mem://h2")
column3: a hard link shares the file's contents

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.link (make Pathon "mem://ghost") (make Pathon "mem://hl") {hard:true}
column3: a hard link to an absent target errors

column1: # §14  touch — create a path if absent and apply {mode}/{mtime}/{atime}/{size}.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.touch (make Pathon "mem://t.txt") drop  (IO.stat (make Pathon "mem://t.txt")).size
column3: touch creates an empty file

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://t.txt") "hello" drop  IO.touch (make Pathon "mem://t.txt") {size:2} drop  (IO.stat (make Pathon "mem://t.txt")).size
column3: touch {size} truncates a file

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.touch (make Pathon "mem://t.txt") {size:-1}
column3: a negative touch size errors

column1: # §15  binary & positioned read/write — {enc:'bytes'} returns Bytes,
#      {offset}/{length} slice a read, a Bytes payload writes verbatim, and
#      {offset} splices a positioned write.
import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://h.txt") "hello" drop  IO.read (make Pathon "mem://h.txt") {offset:1 length:3}
column3: positioned read returns a text slice

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://h.txt") "hello" drop  IO.read (make Pathon "mem://h.txt") {enc:'bytes'}
column3: a binary read returns Bytes

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://b.bin") (convert Bytes "hi") drop  IO.read (make Pathon "mem://b.bin")
column3: writing Bytes stores the raw bytes

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://p.bin") "hello" drop  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://p.bin") (convert Bytes "XY") {offset:1} drop  IO.read (make Pathon "mem://p.bin")
column3: {offset} splices a positioned write

column1: import "aql:io"  context dot __sys dot fs set mem true  IO.write (make Pathon "mem://z.bin") (convert Bytes "a") {offset:-1}
column3: a negative write offset errors

column1: # §7  folder — create a directory, returning its Pathon. IO.folder mutates the
#     HOST filesystem via EffectiveFileOps: the in-memory-FS toggle does not
#     engage through a spec row's context layering, and `make Pathon` collapses
#     a "mem://" scheme so the scheme-routed mem backing can't catch it
#     either. There is therefore no hermetic, deterministic spec surface for
#     it, so it is the one ADR-003 hermetic exemption (see coverage_test.go)
#     and is exercised in the Go tests instead — lang/go/native/folder_test.go.
